(b)(i)
parts.part_stem:
Two long straight parallel wires P and Q are situated a distance 3.1 cm apart, as illustrated in Fig. 8.3.
{{figure:figure_8_3}}
The current in wire P is 6.2 A. The current in wire Q is 8.5 A.
The magnetic flux density $B$ at a distance $x$ from a long straight wire carrying current $I$ is given by the expression
$$B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi x}$$
where $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space.
Calculate:
parts.text: the magnetic flux density at wire Q due to the current in wire P

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the force per unit length, in $\text{N m}^{-1}$, acting on wire Q due to the current in wire P.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The currents in wires P and Q are different in magnitude.
State and explain whether the forces per unit length on the two wires will be different.
